subject.title: Feature: browser tool - expose CDP Network domain for request interception

question: Should OpenClaw expose browser Network/CDP capture or interception to models, and should the first supported contract be passive inspection only or active request interception too?
rationale: The implementation shape changes what authenticated browser traffic a model can observe or manipulate, so code inspection cannot choose the security boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design constrained passive inspection first
options.body: Expose a narrow model-facing request/response inspection API with redaction, permissions, and profile capability gates before considering active mutation.

options.title: Keep only CLI/control APIs for now
options.body: Leave model-facing browser actions unchanged and document the existing `openclaw browser requests` and `responsebody` paths for trusted operator debugging only.

options.title: Allow active interception with explicit policy
options.body: Add active interception only behind a maintainer-approved high-power policy surface and tests for sensitive-data handling across browser profiles.

recommendation.title: Design constrained passive inspection first
recommendation.body: Expose a narrow model-facing request/response inspection API with redaction, permissions, and profile capability gates before considering active mutation.

likelyOwner.reason: The browser plugin runtime and prior browser ownership changes route this security-sensitive API decision most strongly to steipete.
